objectives: Read controlled sentences containing taught short /i/ words accurately.
Identify people, actions, locations and key details from short sentences.
Use text evidence rather than guessing to answer comprehension questions.
concepts: Literal comprehension can identify who, what and where.
Rereading can improve accuracy and confirm meaning.

definitions.definition: Understanding information directly stated in a text.
A word or phrase in the text that supports an answer.
A sentence designed mainly from previously taught sound-spelling patterns.

workedExamples: “Tim sits.” → Who? Tim. What does he do? Sits.
“Tim is in a pit.” → Who? Tim. Where? In a pit.
If “in” is read as “it,” check the final sound and grapheme.
commonMistakes: Answering from memory instead of the sentence.
Guessing from the first letter only.
revisionPoints: Who? What? Where? Find the exact word or phrase.

conceptual: Identify the word that provides the answer.
higherOrderThinking: Explain which text word proves an answer.

formulaOrFactBank: Literal answer = information stated in the sentence
mistakeBasedRevision: in vs it: listen for the final /n/ or /t/.
weakTopicRevision: Reread one sentence slowly and point to the evidence before answering.

activities.name: Sentence detective
steps: Point to the location or detail.

outcomes: Learner reads controlled short /i/ sentences with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner identifies who and what information from a sentence.
Learner identifies a stated location/detail with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner uses text evidence instead of guessing.

Why reread a controlled sentence?
options: To improve accuracy and confirm meaning
